newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X chief says Placer could open bidding.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X chief says Placer could open bidding.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc stands a good chance of opening up the bidding process for the Busang gold project in Indonesia, the chief executive of Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Tuesday.
"I think there is room" for Placer Dome, David Walsh told Reuters in a phone interview.
He said Bre-X's proposed agreement with Barrick Gold Corp to operate the Busang find through a joint venture is not dead.
But the final word on who will work with Bre-X at Busang is up to the Indonesian government, he said.
"I think John Willson and Placer Dome have done a considerable amount of homework, and they're trying to open the process up to an auction, which would be my first choice," Walsh said.
"We still have an agreement with Barrick that isn't dead, but it's subject to the government responding to a couple of items in a joint submission we made," he added.
The proposal with Barrick provides economic terms which would please Bre-X shareholders, he said. But the Placer bid "may be better," he added.
Barrick and Bre-X have not publicized their deal's terms.
Walsh said his company would likely meet with Placer Dome officials next week to discuss details of Placer Dome's offer.
Placer Dome announced early on Tuesday that it wanted to forge a stock-for-stock merger with Bre-X. The Indonesian government has told Bre-X and Barrick to form a deal with each other.
But Walsh said he hopes the Indonesian government will change its mind.
"We will adhere to the government's wishes," he said.
If the bidding process is opened, Placer Dome will probably not be the only company to bid for Bre-X.
"Who's to say there won't be a third proposal or a fourth?" Walsh said.
Teck Corp and Newmont Mining Corp have shown interest in the past.
"I understand that they've been doing their homework," Walsh said. He would not say what other companies were interested.
Any of the companies would be efficient operators of the huge Busang project, he added.
"They all in their own right move a lot of dirt."
